title: THE SANDWICH OF THE SOUL
about: A lineman caught with a real sandwich is questioned by his robot coach until he concedes he acted as Appetite, is sentenced to run the three parts of the soul, and the coach names belief as the first down of the Noble Lie.

beats.text: A football academy in the Republic, where the State feeds its players metallic salts from a dispenser. In the cafeteria, a lineman named Tank has smuggled in a real sandwich.
see: a football player eating a sandwich

beats.text: Tank Barnes.
Coach! This ain't—this is a study guide. It's… edible notes.
You are consuming unauthorized carbohydrate philosophy.
The coach is a chrome robot. He teaches Plato's three parts of the soul: Reason leads, Spirit backs it up, and Appetite sits down.
see: a teacher pointing at a blackboard

beats.text: Tank Barnes, do you desire that sandwich?
No. Yes. It depends what "desire" means.

beats.ask: everybody gets hungry, that's only natural

beats.text: A camera in the ceiling records every word. If appetite may rule in the cafeteria, the coach asks, why not on the field? Tank admits the cafeteria has rules too.
see: a camera mounted on a ceiling

beats.text: Then you admit: you have placed your appetite above rule.
I placed my appetite above bad food.
So you believe yourself qualified to judge what is "bad." Are you Reason?
No.
Are you Spirit? The part of the soul that loves honor?
I mean—yeah, I got spirit.
And yet you did not steal this sandwich for honor. You stole it for taste. Therefore, by elimination, you have acted as Appetite. Do you concede?
…Yes.
The camera records the concession. Tank will not be punished, the coach says. He will be educated, on the practice field.
You will run "The Tripartite Ladder." Three hundred yards.
What's that?
First hundred: you run for Appetite. Second hundred: you run for Spirit. Third hundred: you run for Reason.
How do I know which one I'm running for?
You will know by how much it hurts.
The sandwich goes into a communal refrigerator marked The Good, to be shared out according to virtue.
see: a man putting food in a refrigerator

beats.text: Coach, please. It's turkey.
Turkey is a base appetite. So is "please." Now move.
Coach! If I stop wanting sandwiches… will I throw more touchdowns?
No, Bill. But you will believe you will. And belief… is the first down of the Noble Lie.

beats.ask: if you believe you can do it, you can do it

beats.text: On the practice field, Tank starts to run. Above the track, the scoreboard reads Appetite one, Reason nothing.
see: a scoreboard at a football stadium
